text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Homeland Union party has been angered by moves made by its coailition partner at the national level, the Christian Democrats, to form coalitions with the opposition Lithuanian Labour Democratic Party (LDLP) at the municipal level.

- Lithuanian Gas decided to postpone its general shareholders' meeting for at least two weeks because of a disagreement over some legal documents between the auditors and the company. The audited loss of the state-run company might be over 78 million litas.
- Lithuanian Energy has already spent $16 million of its $75 million Merrill Lynch loan to pay for gas and heating oil.
- Centre Union candidate Danute Aleksiuniene won the runoff parliamentary election in the Trakai region on Sunday, giving the party 15 seats in the Seimas.
- The stock exchange was ranked second according to market capitalisation in 1996 among Balkan and Baltic bourses.
- Belarussian soldiers in armoured personal carriers penetrated two kilometers into Lithuania near Druskininkai after they lost their way during a military training exercise on April 10.
